plcBriefme: Everyday decisions about how we heat our homes, travel and use appliances have a major impact on energy demand, costs, and the transition to a carbon-free economy.
People's energy choices are shaped by habits, social norms and the way that information is presented; not just by prices. Recognising these influences can make policies more effective.

We bring together behavioural evidence, policy examples and research on energy decisions, showing how these insights can support measures ranging from energy labelling to consumer feedback and conservation programmes.
Our work demonstrates how behavioural insights can help policymakers design energy policies that encourage more sustainable choices, while supporting affordable, secure and efficient energy use.

Many of the biggest health challenges depend on everyday behaviours, from diet, exercise and smoking to vaccination, screening and handwashing, making behaviour a central focus for effective public health policy.

Health-related decisions are shaped by social norms, emotions, habits, and the way in which information is presented. Understanding these influences helps policymakers to design more effective interventions.
We bring together behavioural evidence, policy applications and research on health-related decisions, covering areas such as tobacco control, nutrition labelling, physical activity and vaccination.
Our work shows how behavioural insights can support more effective health policies by encouraging healthier choices, improving public engagement and strengthening preventive health measures.

Tax compliance underpins public finances, trust in government and perceptions of fairness. Understanding why people do (or do not) pay their taxes helps policymakers address both intentional and unintentional non-compliance.
People's tax decisions are influenced by trust, social norms, emotions, and how easy it is to understand and fulfil their obligations – not just by audits and financial penalties.
We bring together behavioural evidence, practical guidance and policy examples to show how behavioural insights can improve tax administration, increase compliance and reduce collection costs.
Our work highlights proven approaches, from simplifying tax communications to designing more user-centred systems, that help policymakers make tax compliance easier, fairer and more effective.

column2: Behavioural insights for climate and environment
plcBriefme: Everyday choices about what we buy and eat, how we travel and how we use resources have a major impact on climate change, biodiversity, pollution and the wider environment.

column2: Behavioural insights for climate and environment
plcBriefme: Environmental decisions are shaped by habits, values, social norms and the way in which choices are presented. Behavioural insights help to explain why intentions do not always translate into sustainable actions.

column2: Behavioural insights for climate and environment
plcBriefme: We bring together behavioural evidence, policy applications and research on environmental decision-making, covering areas such as sustainable consumption, product labelling, the circular economy and biodiversity.

column2: Behavioural insights for climate and environment
plcBriefme: Our work shows how behavioural insights can help policymakers design environmental and climate policies that make sustainable choices easier, more attractive and more likely to become everyday behaviour.

column2: Behavioural insights for inclusion and equality
plcBriefme: Attitudes, perceptions and everyday behaviours can reinforce inequality, discrimination and exclusion, making behavioural factors an important consideration when designing policies that promote fairness and equal opportunities.

column2: Behavioural insights for inclusion and equality
plcBriefme: Unconscious biases, social norms and perceptions of fairness influence how people treat others, respond to inequality, and support policies aimed at reducing discrimination and exclusion.

column2: Behavioural insights for inclusion and equality
plcBriefme: We bring together behavioural evidence, policy applications and research on inclusion and equality, covering topics such as discrimination, gender equality, fairness, redistribution and migration.

column2: Behavioural insights for inclusion and equality
plcBriefme: Our research shows how behavioural insights can help policymakers design more effective interventions to reduce bias, promote inclusion, and build fairer, more equitable societies.
People's online decisions affect their privacy, security and wellbeing. They are often influenced by cognitive biases and digital environments that are designed to shape behaviour.
Online users can be persuaded to share personal information or engage in risky behaviour through techniques such as misleading framing, fake social proof and manipulative interface design.
We bring together behavioural research on online decision-making, exploring how people respond to privacy notices, security messages, cookie consent requests and other digital interactions.

Our research show how behavioural insights can help policymakers to design safer digital environments, strengthen online privacy and security, and reduce the effectiveness of manipulative or deceptive practices.

Artificial intelligence is transforming decision-making in areas from education and healthcare to recruitment and finance, making it essential to understand how people interact with and respond to AI systems.
People's trust in AI, perceptions of fairness and willingness to rely on automated recommendations influence whether AI reduces or reinforces bias, discrimination and other unintended harms.
We bring together behavioural research on human-AI interaction, exploring topics such as discrimination, human oversight, trust, education, and the responsible use of AI.
Our research shows how behavioural insights can help policymakers to design AI governance and regulation that promotes fairness, transparency, accountability and meaningful human oversight.

Policymakers need clear, comparable data to understand how countries are responding to economic, social, environmental and geopolitical challenges, including progress against EU priorities and global goals.
Without integrated tools, it is difficult to compare countries or track performance across multiple dimensions such as innovation, sustainability, competitiveness and resilience.
This platform brings together over 150 indices and scoreboards, allowing users to explore, visualise and compare data across countries, topics and time periods through an interactive format.
It supports evidence-based policymaking by making complex datasets accessible through country profiles, scoreboards, correlation tools and thematic comparisons aligned with EU and UN priorities.

Culture and creativity contribute to economic growth, social wellbeing and urban development. Policymakers need robust evidence to understand how cities are performing in these terms, and where investment can have the greatest impact.
Comparing cities can be difficult, because cultural and creative strengths are diverse and not easily captured by traditional economic indicators alone.

Our interactive tool benchmarks almost 200 European cities using quantitative and qualitative data, enabling users to compare performance across multiple dimensions of cultural, social and economic vitality.
It helps policymakers to identify local strengths, learn from comparable cities, and support evidence-based strategies to foster culture, creativity and sustainable urban development.
Achieving gender equality is essential for a fair, prosperous and inclusive society, but measuring progress requires reliable evidence across many different areas of policy and public life.
Policymakers need accessible data to understand where progress is being made, identify persistent inequalities, and compare outcomes across Member States over time.
This interactive portal brings together indicators aligned with the EU Gender Equality Strategy, allowing users to explore trends, compare countries and examine progress across key policy objectives.
It supports evidence-based policymaking by making gender equality data easy to access, visualise and use for monitoring, evaluation and policy development.
Inequality extends beyond income, affecting health, education, work, safety, political participation and many other aspects of people's lives. It is essential to understand its multiple dimensions.
Focusing on a single measure can lead policymakers to overlook important disparities between different groups and life domains, limiting their ability to identify where action is most needed.
Our interactive framework brings together hundreds of indicators covering ten areas of life, enabling users to explore, compare and analyse inequalities across EU countries and population groups.
It supports evidence-based policymaking by providing comprehensive data and visualisation tools to monitor inequalities, identify trends and inform more inclusive policies.

Fraud targeting the EU budget undermines public finances and trust, making it essential for authorities to identify suspicious patterns of behaviour quickly, and strengthen the protection of the EU's financial interests.
Large and complex datasets can conceal fraudulent activity, requiring specialised statistical methods and analytical tools to detect unusual patterns that would otherwise be difficult to identify.

THESEUS develops and applies innovative statistical methods and web-based analytical tools that help anti-fraud experts monitor international trade data, investigate anomalies and support fraud detection.

It strengthens the analytical capabilities of the European Anti-Fraud Office and its partners in the Member States by providing secure tools, shared methods and evidence to support more effective fraud prevention and investigation.

column2: HERMES tool for international trade codes
plcBriefme: Accurate product classification is essential for customs, tariffs and trade statistics, but product codes change over time, making it difficult to interpret historical trade data consistently.

column2: HERMES tool for international trade codes
plcBriefme: Policymakers, customs authorities and businesses need reliable ways to trace how product classifications have evolved, and understand the relationships between old and new codes.

column2: HERMES tool for international trade codes
plcBriefme: HERMES is an interactive tool that tracks changes in EU trade nomenclature, allowing users to explore product code histories through searchable graphs, tables and hierarchical visualisations.

column2: HERMES tool for international trade codes
plcBriefme: It supports customs, trade analysis and fraud detection by making complex classification changes easier to understand, navigate and apply across different time periods.

column2: Flexible Statistics and Data Analysis (FSDA) toolbox
plcBriefme: Policymakers and researchers increasingly rely on complex datasets, requiring robust methods to identify patterns, test models and produce reliable evidence for decision-making.

column2: Flexible Statistics and Data Analysis (FSDA) toolbox
plcBriefme: Standard analytical techniques may struggle with large, diverse or unusual datasets containing outliers, making specialised statistical methods and clear visualisation essential for accurate analysis.

column2: Flexible Statistics and Data Analysis (FSDA) toolbox
plcBriefme: The FSDA toolbox is an open statistical software package, providing advanced methods, interactive visualisations and extensive documentation to support flexible data analysis.

column2: Flexible Statistics and Data Analysis (FSDA) toolbox
plcBriefme: It helps analysts to apply robust statistical techniques more effectively, improving the quality, transparency and reproducibility of evidence used in research and policymaking.

column2: SOCRATES tool for Social Multi-Criteria Evaluation (SMCE)
plcBriefme: Policymakers often need to balance economic, social and environmental objectives when choosing between policy options. Transparent and structured decision-making is essential.

column2: SOCRATES tool for Social Multi-Criteria Evaluation (SMCE)
plcBriefme: Comparing complex policy choices can be difficult because different stakeholders value outcomes differently, and evidence may involve multiple, sometimes conflicting, criteria.

column2: SOCRATES tool for Social Multi-Criteria Evaluation (SMCE)
plcBriefme: SOCRATES is a software tool that supports the prior impact assessment of policies by applying the Social Multi-Criteria Evaluation framework, to compare policy options in a transparent and systematic way.

column2: SOCRATES tool for Social Multi-Criteria Evaluation (SMCE)
plcBriefme: It helps policymakers and analysts to improve the transparency of policy formulation, make evidence-informed decisions and find compromise solutions.

column2: SMCE@EC Social Multi-Criteria Evaluation for policymakers
plcBriefme: High-quality impact assessments depend on transparent methods and consistent evidence.

column2: SMCE@EC Social Multi-Criteria Evaluation for policymakers
plcBriefme: Applying complex analytical frameworks can be challenging for policymakers. They need practical guidance on when and how to use decision-analysis methods within the European Commission's impact assessment process.

column2: SMCE@EC Social Multi-Criteria Evaluation for policymakers
plcBriefme: SMCE@EC is a knowledge platform that explains how to apply Social Multi-Criteria Evaluation and the SOCRATES tool throughout the Commission's impact assessment workflow.

column2: SMCE@EC Social Multi-Criteria Evaluation for policymakers
plcBriefme: It helps Commission staff to integrate structured decision-analysis methods into policy development, supporting more transparent, consistent and evidence-informed impact assessments.

Policymakers and researchers need timely insights into global events such as health crises, conflicts, disasters and security risks, which are often first reflected in large volumes of news and online reporting.
Making sense of rapidly growing multilingual information streams is challenging without advanced tools that can automatically detect, classify and summarise relevant developments.
The Europe Media Monitor (EMM) is a research capacity that is able to analyse high-volume news and text data using AI techniques such as topic detection, entity recognition and framing analysis.
It supports early warning, situational awareness and research by turning unstructured media content into structured insights in policy-relevant domains such as public health, safety and security.

column2: Detecting framing and persuasion techniques: overview
plcBriefme: Information in the news and online media can influence how people think and act, often through subtle framing and persuasion techniques that operate below the level of conscious awareness.

column2: Detecting framing and persuasion techniques: overview
plcBriefme: In an environment of constant information overload, it is increasingly important for policymakers and citizens to recognise how language can shape perceptions, attitudes and decision-making.

column2: Detecting framing and persuasion techniques: overview
plcBriefme: Our research focuses on how persuasion and framing are used in multilingual news content, using computational methods to detect patterns in large-scale media data.

column2: Detecting framing and persuasion techniques: overview
plcBriefme: It helps to improve media analysis and supports transparency, public understanding and more informed responses to influence in digital environments.

column2: Support for EU migration management: overview
plcBriefme: Migration and asylum are complex policy areas that are shaped by global instability, demographic change and irregular mobility, requiring reliable evidence to support effective and humane decision-making.

column2: Support for EU migration management: overview
plcBriefme: Policymakers need an understanding of migration flows, drivers and future trends to design policies on asylum, returns, legal pathways and cooperation with partner countries.

column2: Support for EU migration management: overview
plcBriefme: Our project supports the EU’s Pact on Migration and Asylum by providing analysis, foresight and evidence on migration dynamics and related policy challenges.

column2: Support for EU migration management: overview
plcBriefme: It helps to strengthen EU migration governance by improving preparedness, informing policy design and supporting coordination between Member States and international partners.

Migration is shaped by interconnected economic, social, political and environmental factors, and understanding these drivers is essential for designing effective and forward-looking migration policies.

Without a clear understanding of why people move and how migration patterns evolve, policymakers risk relying on incomplete information when planning for future labour needs, asylum systems and cooperation with partner countries.
Our project analyses the underlying drivers of migration, and fills knowledge gaps by combining research evidence, data and foresight to better understand migration dynamics.
It supports more anticipatory and evidence-informed policymaking, strengthening the EU’s capacity to anticipate migration trends and design policies that respond to real-world mobility patterns.

Europe's demographic landscape is evolving through increased longevity, low fertility and migration, each contributing to changes in population size, age structure and regional distribution. These trends present both opportunities and challenges for healthcare, labour markets, housing, regional development and long-term policy planning.

Demographic research provides population projections, scenario modelling and data on fertility, mortality and migration. It helps policymakers anticipate future developments, assess policy options and better understand how demographic trends differ across regions and over time.

We provide a range of EU knowledge resources, including the Atlas of Demography, modelling tools, statistics and reports developed by the Joint Research Centre, to support the analysis and visualisation of population change across Europe.

These resources help to inform evidence-based policymaking in areas such as health, employment, migration, housing and regional development. By increasing understanding of demographic trends, they support the design of policies that respond to changing population structures, address labour market needs and promote resilient and thriving communities across the EU.

column2: Attitudes and perceptions around migration and demography: overview
plcBriefme: Migration and demographic change can affect social cohesion, trust in institutions and perceptions of inequality, making public attitudes a key policy issue for managing integration, communication strategies and long-term demographic planning across societies and political systems.

column2: Attitudes and perceptions around migration and demography: overview
plcBriefme: Research in this area helps policymakers to understand how opinions form, how media narratives spread and how misinformation influences behaviour, enabling more effective communication strategies, targeted interventions and improved public engagement on sensitive migration topics.

column2: Attitudes and perceptions around migration and demography: overview
plcBriefme: We analyse public and media discourse on migration and demographics, identifying patterns of disinformation and providing evidence, methodologies and analytical resources to support the detection and understanding of false narratives, while also mapping attitudes and concerns that influence societal cohesion and political debate.

column2: Attitudes and perceptions around migration and demography: overview
plcBriefme: Our findings support EU-level efforts to improve digital and media literacy, strengthen resilience to disinformation, and design 'pre-bunking' strategies that reduce the impact of misleading narratives before they spread widely across online and offline information environments.

Migration is influenced by a wide range of drivers, including economic, social and political factors, with implications for population change, labour markets and integration. Having reliable global data is essential for designing fair and effective migration, asylum and development policies across interconnected countries.

Research tools in this field help policymakers to explore migration patterns across countries, identify emerging challenges such as displacement or irregular migration, and support evidence-informed policymaking.

The Atlas of Migration provides harmonised, validated data for 198 countries and territories, combining indicators on population, legal and irregular migration, asylum, integration and labour markets, supported by interactive visualisations and regularly updated country profiles.

It enables EU and global policymakers to monitor migration trends, assess policy impacts across regions, and design coordinated responses informed by comparable data on displacement, mobility patterns and socio-economic conditions.

Europe’s changing population patterns affect labour supply, healthcare needs and migration trends, making an understanding of demography essential for planning services, infrastructure and long-term fiscal sustainability across ageing and diversifying societies.

Research in this area helps policymakers to connect demographic trends with social and economic outcomes, improving foresight and enabling coordinated responses to ageing, regional population decline and the changing workforce.

The Atlas of Demography brings together validated data and interactive visualisations on European demographic change, linking population trends to impact areas such as health, labour and regional migration, to support accessible, policy-relevant understanding across multiple domains.
It complements the European Commission’s Demography Toolbox by enabling evidence-informed policymaking and improving the shared understanding of population shifts.

Effective policymaking depends on collaboration across teams and institutions, as fragmented communication and weak coordination can reduce efficiency, slow implementation and limit the ability to address complex, cross-cutting policy challenges.

Research in behavioural and organisational sciences helps to identify what drives cooperation, improves decision-making and supports better team dynamics by examining trust, communication and shared purpose in public sector environments.

Our work helps to develop practical approaches to collaborative policymaking, including digital collaboration tools, organisational practices and guidance informed by behavioural science, to improve how teams work together within the European Commission.

It includes the Collaboration Hub and a set of twelve principles for better collaboration, offering evidence-informed guidance to strengthen coordination, knowledge-sharing and collective problem-solving across public administrations.

column2: The Science Behind the Way we Work: overview
plcBriefme: The effectiveness of public administration depends on how people work together, adapt to change and manage uncertainty, making organisational behaviour a key factor in productivity, wellbeing and policy delivery across complex institutional environments.

column2: The Science Behind the Way we Work: overview
plcBriefme: Research in cognitive, behavioural and organisational sciences helps to explain how trust forms, how people respond to change and how collaboration and conflict can be managed, to improve decision-making and organisational performance.

column2: The Science Behind the Way we Work: overview
plcBriefme: The Science Behind the Way we Work series translates scientific evidence into practical guidance on workplace issues such as trust, change management, conflict resolution, meeting design and office environments, to improve day-to-day functioning in public sector organisations.

column2: The Science Behind the Way we Work: overview
plcBriefme: It supports more effective public administration by encouraging evidence-informed working practices that strengthen collaboration, reduce friction and improve adaptability in rapidly changing organisational contexts.

column2: TIM analytics tools for interpreting large datasets
plcBriefme: Policy decisions increasingly rely on analysing vast datasets (e.g. of patient information), making it difficult to identify patterns across large information sources without advanced digital tools and structured data analysis methods.

column2: TIM analytics tools for interpreting large datasets
plcBriefme: Research in text mining and AI for data analytics helps to improve evidence-informed decision-making in complex, fast-moving policy areas, by enabling analysts to detect early signals in data or deal with the complexities of multi-dimensional datasets.

column2: TIM analytics tools for interpreting large datasets
plcBriefme: TIM analytics tools extract and analyse information from various datasets (e.g. scientific publications, patent registers, EU research projects, news feeds) combining multiple data sources into practical tools to e.g. map innovation or detect emerging technological developments.

column2: TIM analytics tools for interpreting large datasets
plcBriefme: They support EU institutions by improving foresight capabilities and strengthening policy responses to innovation and research-driven change.

column2: AI for the public sector: overview
plcBriefme: Artificial intelligence is transforming how public administrations deliver services, helping to manage resources and supporting decision-making, creating opportunities to improve efficiency while creating important organisational, technical and governance challenges.

column2: AI for the public sector: overview
plcBriefme: Research helps policymakers to assess where AI can add value, understand the risks of adoption and develop approaches that support trustworthy, effective and responsible use across different areas of government.

column2: AI for the public sector: overview
plcBriefme: Our work examines how AI, including generative AI, is used in the public sector, providing evidence, frameworks and practical guidance on adoption across areas such as service delivery, planning, monitoring and law enforcement.

column2: AI for the public sector: overview
plcBriefme: It supports EU policymaking by informing strategies for trustworthy AI adoption and helping public administrations move from small-scale experiments to coordinated, evidence-informed implementation.

Artificial intelligence is reshaping healthcare and wellbeing by supporting research, diagnosis and service delivery, while raising important questions about safety, effectiveness, ethics and the responsible use of health data.
Research helps policymakers understand where AI delivers real benefits, assess potential risks and identify the conditions needed for safe, trustworthy and effective adoption across health systems.

Our work examines AI applications in health and wellbeing, bringing together evidence on medical care, digital health technologies, mental health and healthcare management, to inform policy and practice.
It supports EU policies on AI and health by providing evidence that helps guide responsible innovation, improve healthcare delivery and strengthen public trust in emerging technologies.

column2: AI for transparency and oversight: overview
plcBriefme: As AI becomes more widely used, policymakers need ways to maximise its benefits while managing risks related to safety, fairness, accountability and public trust across different sectors and applications.

column2: AI for transparency and oversight: overview
plcBriefme: Research helps in developing methods to assess AI systems, evaluate risks and support regulatory approaches that keep pace with rapid technological change while protecting people and fundamental rights.

column2: AI for transparency and oversight: overview
plcBriefme: Our work provides scientific evidence on AI governance, including benchmarking, risk evaluation, standards and the assessment of general-purpose AI models, while supporting implementation of the EU AI Act.

column2: AI for transparency and oversight: overview
plcBriefme: It helps policymakers and industry develop trustworthy AI by strengthening oversight, improving regulatory tools and promoting consistent approaches to evaluating AI systems and their impacts.

Artificial intelligence is changing how research is conducted, accelerating discovery and expanding access to knowledge while raising questions about transparency, ethics, participation and the future of scientific practice.

Research helps policymakers and researchers understand how AI is transforming science, assess emerging opportunities and risks and develop policies that support innovation while safeguarding research quality and integrity.

Our work analyses the use of AI throughout the scientific process, examining its implications for research, society and the economy while providing evidence to inform the European Commission’s AI in Science Strategy.
It supports evidence-informed policies that encourage responsible AI adoption in research, strengthening Europe's scientific competitiveness and innovation capacity.

Innovation depends on connections between researchers, businesses, investors and public organisations. Strong innovation ecosystems help turn research into practical solutions, supporting competitiveness, economic growth and societal challenges.

Research helps to identify effective approaches to designing and managing innovation ecosystems, showing how organisations, funding and support services can improve knowledge-sharing and technology transfer.
We bring together guidance, tools, studies and projects on innovation ecosystems, including from technology transfer offices, incubators and accelerators.

Our work supports policymakers and practitioners in strengthening innovation systems, improving research commercialisation, and developing effective support structures at the regional, national and European level.
Promising research often needs financial support to reach the market. Well-designed funding and investment tools can help bridge the gap between research, innovation and commercial use.
Research helps to identify effective financing models, showing how public and private funding can support technology transfer while reducing risks for innovators and investors.
We bring together guidance, studies and tools on technology transfer finance, covering proof-of-concept funding, innovation vouchers, equity, debt and intellectual property financing.
Our work supports evidence-informed policies to strengthen innovation funding, improve commercialisation pathways and expand access to finance for research-based innovation.

Turning research into innovation requires skills in areas such as intellectual property, business development and commercial partnerships. Building this capacity helps research organisations to provide greater economic and societal value.

Research can identify the knowledge, skills and support needed for effective technology transfer, helping research organisations to strengthen their innovation processes and improve their collaboration with industry.

We bring together guidance, tools and projects on capacity-building for technology transfer, covering technology assessment, intellectual property management, business development and negotiating commercial agreements.
Our work supports policies that strengthen technology transfer capabilities, helping research organisations to translate scientific knowledge into innovation and wider public benefit.

column2: The geopolitical dimension of digital sovereignty
plcBriefme: Europe depends on digital technologies, infrastructure and data beyond its physical borders, exposing it to shocks caused by geopolitical shifts, disruptions in supply chains and changes in regulations and norms around the world.

column2: The geopolitical dimension of digital sovereignty
plcBriefme: Research can help to identify these dependencies and risks, as well as the factors that can increase the EU’s agency in addressing them.

column2: The geopolitical dimension of digital sovereignty
plcBriefme: Our multi-layered analytical framework maps the strategic dilemmas that arise in the digital space. These include the trade-off between de-risking critical infrastructures and preserving interconnectedness; the balance between economic statecraft and global market integration, and the challenge of strengthening social cohesion without undermining individual liberties.

column2: The geopolitical dimension of digital sovereignty
plcBriefme: Our work aims to make policymakers aware of different approaches to digital sovereignty and their trade-offs, taking into account their implications for innovation, security and alignment with EU values.

The EU’s dependence on foreign critical technologies (e.g. in AI and quantum computing) is central to discussions of digital sovereignty. Without clear data, evaluating and addressing these dependencies is challenging.
Research can help in providing frameworks of indicators that allow for easier mapping and analysis of the critical interconnections between countries in key digital domains.

We provide quantitative evidence to policymakers on key aspects of digital sovereignty across Europe. This includes through our Ecosystem Measurement Framework, which maps and analyses critical interconnections between countries, in important areas for digital sovereignty. It focuses on identifying and monitoring critical dependencies and strategic opportunities in key digital domains (AI, quantum, semiconductors etc), considering dependency levels, strategic indispensability, control, capabilities and resilience.
In doing so, our aim is to provide policymakers with consistent quantitative evidence.

column2: EU policies and the bioeconomy: overview
plcBriefme: The EU Bioeconomy Strategy has a cross-sectoral character and holistic perspective and is linked to many sectoral policies. Coordinated policies are needed to support the transition to a competitive and sustainable bioeconomy.

column2: EU policies and the bioeconomy: overview
plcBriefme: Research can help to assess how bio-based solutions can contribute to progress towards climate, environmental and economic goals, informing policies across sectors such as agriculture, industry, energy and innovation.

column2: EU policies and the bioeconomy: overview
plcBriefme: We bring together key policies and funding instruments related to bioeconomy.

column2: EU policies and the bioeconomy: overview
plcBriefme: This constantly updated list helps policymakers to understand the broader policy landscape in this area, identify synergies across sectors and support coherent bioeconomy strategies at the EU, national and regional level.

Europe depends on digital technologies that are increasingly important for economic security, public services and competitiveness. Reducing critical dependencies while remaining open to international cooperation has become a key policy challenge.

Research can help to clarify complex concepts, identify strategic risks and opportunities, and provide evidence to help policymakers balance innovation, resilience, competitiveness and democratic values in the digital space.

We set out a common framework for understanding EU digital sovereignty, examining governance, digital infrastructure and markets, while highlighting priorities such as strategic investment, secure data ecosystems, interoperability and digital skills.

Our work supports policymakers in developing coordinated digital strategies that strengthen resilience, reduce external dependencies, and promote an open, competitive and values-based European digital ecosystem.

Forests can help to reduce climate change by storing carbon and providing renewable materials that replace more carbon-intensive alternatives. Sustainable management is essential to maintain these climate benefits over time.

Research can help in assessing how forests, sustainable land management and the use of wood resources contribute to progress towards climate goals, identifying trade-offs and informing more effective climate and forestry policies.
We bring together evidence, briefs, datasets and tools on forest-based bioeconomy, carbon storage and sustainable forest management, alongside related EU policies and initiatives.
Our work supports evidence-informed decision-making on forestry, land use and climate policy, while helping to protect forest resilience and biodiversity.

Measuring progress is essential for understanding whether the bioeconomy is delivering economic, social and environmental benefits. Reliable data helps policymakers to monitor trends and assess the impact of policy decisions.

Research can help in developing indicators and monitoring frameworks that track progress over time, supporting evidence-informed policymaking and improving understanding of complex sustainability challenges.

We provide an interactive monitoring system with indicators, dashboards and downloadable data covering the EU bioeconomy, linked to the EU Bioeconomy Strategy, the Sustainable Development Goals and the European Green Deal.
Our work helps policymakers to monitor progress, compare trends across countries and develop more evidence-informed bioeconomy policies at the EU and national level.

Cancer is a leading cause of illness and death across Europe. Having comparable data is essential for understanding trends, planning services and evaluating policies to improve prevention, diagnosis and care.
Research can provide the evidence that is needed to measure the burden of cancer, monitor changes over time and assess the impact of public health interventions in different countries.

We offers comparable European data, visualisations and factsheets on cancer incidence, mortality, survival and prevalence, helping users to explore trends and differences across different European populations.
Our work supports evidence-informed cancer policies by enabling monitoring, international comparisons and better planning of prevention, treatment and healthcare services.
Cancer outcomes vary between population groups and countries. Understanding these inequalities helps policymakers to target action and improve prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care.
Research can identify where inequalities exist, how they change over time and which policies can help reduce differences in cancer outcomes across populations.

The European Cancer Inequalities Registry brings together data, country profiles, analytical reports and factsheets to explore inequalities in cancer prevention and care across multiple social and demographic groups.
It supports evidence-based policies by helping to monitor inequalities, compare progress across countries and identify priorities for more equitable cancer care.
Cancer remains a major health challenge across Europe, requiring coordinated policymaking around prevention, early detection, treatment and care to reduce mortality and improve quality of life.
Research and policy analysis can help to identify effective interventions, guide resource allocation and support cooperation between countries in tackling shared cancer challenges.
We bring together analysis of EU cancer initiatives, including Europe’s Beating Cancer Plan and the Horizon Europe Mission on Cancer, alongside related programmes.
Our work supports coherent EU-wide policymaking around cancer, by linking strategies, funding programmes and institutions that are working to reduce the impact of cancer.

Soil health underpins food production, climate regulation and ecosystems, but large areas in Europe are degraded, threatening environmental sustainability, agricultural productivity and long-term economic resilience.
Research can help in measuring soil conditions, tracking degradation and carbon storage, and providing evidence on how land use and management practices affect soil health over time.
We bring together EU-wide monitoring systems, including the LUCAS Soil Module, to collect data on soil properties, land use and degradation trends across Member States.
Our work supports policymakers by providing indicators, dashboards and evidence tools to guide soil protection, land-use planning and restoration policies across Europe.

Air pollution remains a major public health and environmental issue in Europe. Reliable assessment tools are needed to design effective policies and reduce harmful emissions across sectors and regions.

Research can help in comparing air quality models, identifying uncertainties and improving understanding of emissions, pollutant dispersion and exposure, supporting more accurate and consistent decision-making.
We provide benchmarking tools and methods for comparing air quality models, including emissions and their concentrations, using standardised datasets and evaluation approaches.
Our work supports better air quality governance by identifying best practices, improving modelling consistency across Member States, and informing EU policies around the reduction of air pollution.

column2: Testing methods to detect food fraud
plcBriefme: Food fraud is any intentional deception of consumers around food. It can involve replacing more expensive ingredients with cheaper ones, lying about the origin of food or production processes, or tampering with records such as best-by dates. Food fraud undermines consumer trust, safety and fair markets. It can distort prices, harm legitimate producers and mislead consumers about what they are eating and where it comes from.

column2: Testing methods to detect food fraud
plcBriefme: Research can help in providing reliable methods for detecting food fraud.

column2: Testing methods to detect food fraud
plcBriefme: We have developed, and make available, reliable tests that control laboratories and industry can use to identify cases of food fraud.

column2: Testing methods to detect food fraud
plcBriefme: Our work supports policymakers, regulators and industry by helping to improve the monitoring and prevention of fraud, and the enforcement of anti-fraud measures, across food supply chains at the national, EU and global level.

Global food systems are putting unsustainable pressure on the environment, generating around 30% of global greenhouse gas emissions and driving biodiversity loss, while simultaneously failing to deliver healthy diets for all, creating urgent policy challenges.
Research can help in identifying pathways for more sustainable food systems, including improved production methods, reduced waste, healthier diets, and fairer value chains across different countries.
We provide evidence and curated knowledge on these topics, as well as an overview of EU and global policies and initiatives on sustainable food systems.
Our work supports policymakers in designing integrated food system strategies that improve nutrition, reduce environmental impact and strengthen resilience across supply chains and populations.

column2: Food crises and food and nutrition security: overview
plcBriefme: Millions of people face hunger and food insecurity worldwide, driven by conflict, climate shocks and economic instability, creating urgent humanitarian and long-term development challenges.

column2: Food crises and food and nutrition security: overview
plcBriefme: Research can help in measuring food insecurity, identifying vulnerable populations and understanding drivers of food insecurity such as trade disruptions and climate impacts, to support better crisis response and prevention.

column2: Food crises and food and nutrition security: overview
plcBriefme: We bring together data and analysis on global food crises, nutrition challenges and food security trends, including links to SDG monitoring and international assessments.

column2: Food crises and food and nutrition security: overview
plcBriefme: Our work supports coordinated EU and global responses by improving evidence for emergency action, long-term resilience and policies aimed at reducing hunger and malnutrition.
Mental health conditions such as depression and anxiety are major public health challenges, affecting quality of life, productivity and healthcare provision across Europe.
Research can help in identifying risk factors, effective prevention strategies and population-level trends, supporting earlier intervention and better mental health outcomes.
We provide evidence and analysis related to the promotion of mental health and the prevention of depression, work-related stress and dementia, their risk factors, and policies to address them.
Our work supports policymakers in designing prevention strategies, improving well-being and strengthening public health responses to mental health challenges.

column2: Societal impacts of non-communicable disease: overview
plcBriefme: Non-communicable diseases place a major burden on societies through illness, premature death and long-term care needs, affecting economic productivity, social systems and health equity across population groups.

column2: Societal impacts of non-communicable disease: overview
plcBriefme: Research can help in measuring disease burdens, identifying inequalities and quantifying economic and social costs, supporting more effective prevention and resource allocation across health systems.

column2: Societal impacts of non-communicable disease: overview
plcBriefme: We provide evidence on the societal impacts of non-communicable diseases, including cost analyses, disease burden studies and insights into the determinants of disease across different population groups.

column2: Societal impacts of non-communicable disease: overview
plcBriefme: Our work supports policymakers in recognising the burden of preventable non-communicable diseases, making the case for stronger prevention strategies to reduce the wider social and economic impacts of non-communicable diseases and address inequalities.

column2: Risk factors for non-communicable diseases: overview
plcBriefme: Many non-communicable diseases are driven by lifestyle factors such as diet, physical inactivity, tobacco use and alcohol consumption, creating major but preventable health burdens across Europe.

column2: Risk factors for non-communicable diseases: overview
plcBriefme: Research can help in identifying how different behaviours affect health, informing prevention strategies that can reduce disease risk and improve population well-being.

column2: Risk factors for non-communicable diseases: overview
plcBriefme: We provide evidence on key risk factors, including poor nutrition, physical inactivity, smoking and alcohol consumption, along with summaries of health impacts and related EU data and policies.

column2: Risk factors for non-communicable diseases: overview
plcBriefme: Our work supports policymakers in designing prevention measures, promoting healthier behaviours and reducing the long-term burden of chronic diseases on health systems and societies.
Pesticides support agricultural productivity but can also harm human health, biodiversity, soil and water quality, creating a need for careful regulation and risk reduction across Europe.
Research can help in assessing pesticide use, exposure and environmental impacts, improving understanding of risks and supporting more precise, data-driven regulation and monitoring systems.
We provide scientific analysis, EU-wide datasets on pesticide use, emissions and risks, and monitoring tools developed by the Joint Research Centre.

Our work supports policymakers in reducing pesticide risks, improving environmental monitoring and working towards EU goals on sustainable agriculture, biodiversity protection and pollution reduction.

Untreated or poorly treated wastewater can harm ecosystems, spread pollutants and affect public health. Effective treatment is essential for safe water, healthy cities and climate-resilient urban development.
Research can help in assessing pollution levels, treatment effectiveness and environmental impacts, supporting better design of wastewater systems and more effective water protection policies.

We provide evidence and analysis in support of the EU wastewater policy and the Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive, including advanced treatment, pollution control, energy neutrality and water reuse in cities.
Our work supports policymakers in improving water resilience, reducing pollution from urban areas and promoting sustainable wastewater management across Europe.

Water scarcity and drought are increasing across Europe, threatening agriculture, ecosystems and economic stability. Efficient water use is essential for climate resilience and long-term resource security.
Research can help in assessing risks, setting quality standards and evaluating potential uses of treated wastewater, supporting safe and effective water reuse in different sectors.
We provide evidence and analysis in support of EU water reuse policy and work on standards, risk management and applications of treated wastewater in agriculture, industry and landscape irrigation.
Our work supports policymakers in scaling safe water reuse, improving water security and reducing pressure on freshwater resources under climate and demand pressures.
Biodiversity loss threatens ecosystems, food systems and climate stability, making reliable global monitoring essential for informed conservation and sustainable development policies.

Research can provide standardised indicators and datasets to measure species numbers, ecosystems and environmental pressures, helping to compare trends across countries and track progress against global biodiversity goals.
We offer a global biodiversity data platform with country profiles, interactive maps, downloadable reports, APIs and tools to explore and analyse biodiversity and environmental pressure data.

Our work supports policymakers in reporting on progress, identifying risks and aligning national and international biodiversity action with frameworks such as the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.

column2: The Biodiversity Information System for Europe
plcBriefme: Effective biodiversity policy depends on access to reliable, up-to-date information. Bringing data and evidence together helps to support coordinated conservation efforts across Europe.

column2: The Biodiversity Information System for Europe
plcBriefme: Research generates the data, indicators and knowledge needed to understand biodiversity trends, evaluate policies and guide conservation and ecosystem management.

column2: The Biodiversity Information System for Europe
plcBriefme: The Biodiversity Information System for Europe (BISE) provides a single access point to European biodiversity information, bringing together policy, data, research, maps and national reporting under one platform.

column2: The Biodiversity Information System for Europe
plcBriefme: It supports policymakers by improving access to evidence, strengthening biodiversity reporting and enabling more informed environmental decision-making across the EU.

column2: EU policies and Earth Observation: overview
plcBriefme: Policy challenges require cross-sector action at a large scale, while assessing the effectiveness of policy responses calls for accurate, timely feedback.

column2: EU policies and Earth Observation: overview
plcBriefme: Earth Observation (EO) can help with this, using satellites and sensors to monitor land, oceans and atmosphere. The collected data can inform decision-making across a range of policy areas – from environment and agriculture to disaster response, transport and security.

column2: EU policies and Earth Observation: overview
plcBriefme: We map EU policy areas from an EO perspective and provide real-life examples of how EO data can be used. A series of deep-dive assessments are carried out to address this specific objective.

column2: EU policies and Earth Observation: overview
plcBriefme: Our work helps policymakers to understand what EO can offer, matching specific policy needs to the available tools and data, and guiding future investment in Europe's space and monitoring capabilities.
Many policy challenges require cross-border action at a large scale. Accurate, timely feedback can be very useful in assessing the effectiveness of policies.
Copernicus, Europe’s eyes on Earth, can help in providing this feedback.

Copernicus is the Earth Observation component of the EU Space Programme. It provides a wealth of data (processed, analysed and delivered through the Copernicus thematic services), covering land, marine and atmospheric environments, as well as climate change, security and emergency management.

Our work helps to turn the raw data from Copernicus into actionable information to support decision-makers across a range of sectors, including public policy, research and innovation, helping in the development of sustainable and secure policies.

column2: ELINDER: the nuclear decommissioning training programme
plcBriefme: Nuclear facilities must be safely dismantled at the end of their operational life. This requires specialist expertise to protect workers, the public and the environment while managing complex technical challenges.

column2: ELINDER: the nuclear decommissioning training programme
plcBriefme: Research and training help in developing the knowledge, skills and best practices needed for safe, efficient and consistent decommissioning across different countries and facilities.

column2: ELINDER: the nuclear decommissioning training programme
plcBriefme: The ELINDER training programme provides introductory, specialised and e-learning courses on nuclear decommissioning, delivered through partnerships between the Joint Research Centre, universities and technical institutes.

column2: ELINDER: the nuclear decommissioning training programme
plcBriefme: It supports capacity-building by promoting shared qualifications, strengthening technical expertise and encouraging common approaches to nuclear decommissioning across Europe.

column2: The nuclear decommissioning waste management programme: overview
plcBriefme: Decommissioning nuclear facilities and managing radioactive waste are long-term challenges that require careful planning to protect people, the environment and future generations.

column2: The nuclear decommissioning waste management programme: overview
plcBriefme: Research can help to improve decommissioning methods, waste management practices and safety procedures, supporting more effective and consistent approaches across nuclear sites.

column2: The nuclear decommissioning waste management programme: overview
plcBriefme: The Joint Research Centre's Nuclear Decommissioning and Waste Management Programme covers the safe shutdown of facilities and management of radioactive waste across multiple European sites.

column2: The nuclear decommissioning waste management programme: overview
plcBriefme: It supports policymakers and practitioners by sharing knowledge and experience that strengthens nuclear safety, waste management and decommissioning practices across Europe.
Understanding the full environmental impact of products is essential for designing effective sustainability policies and supporting more informed production and consumption decisions.
Life cycle assessment is an effective way of measuring environmental impacts from raw materials to disposal, helping to compare options and identify opportunities to reduce environmental harm.
We explain life cycle assessment methods and provide guidance and tools to support their use in business and policymaking, including applications for plastics and ecotoxicity.
Our work supports evidence-informed policies on the circular economy, sustainable products and environmental impact assessment across a wide range of EU policy areas.
Everyday choices in areas such as food, transport and housing have significant environmental impacts. Measuring these impacts can support more sustainable consumption and policy design.
Research uses Life Cycle Assessment to estimate environmental impacts across the full life cycle of products, providing a more complete picture than direct emissions alone.
This resource offers an interactive calculator that estimates the environmental footprint of personal consumption across five lifestyle areas, using 16 environmental impact indicators.

It supports policymakers by demonstrating how consumption patterns affect progress towards sustainability goals, and by promoting evidence-based approaches to responsible consumption and environmental awareness.
Fast-moving technologies such as AI, blockchain and neurotechnology can create major opportunities, but they can also lead to challenges.
Strategic foresight research can support policymakers in their efforts to respond to these changes in technology in a timely and effective way, by providing relevant information and analysis.
Our work involves systematically scanning for emerging, disruptive and/ or critical technologies, assessing their potential impact, and identifying what could influence their uptake.

By involving diverse stakeholders in collective-intelligence exercises, we help EU policymakers to anticipate technological developments and their implications – including their associated opportunities, challenges and risks, both in the short and long term.

Today’s crises are increasingly interconnected, making conventional risk assessment insufficient. Policymakers need diverse sources of insights to increase resilience to adverse events, by anticipating and preparing for global shocks and disasters.

In this context, foresight research and systems thinking can complement traditional risk assessment by helping to identify emerging threats, how they are connected, and whether early action could reduce or prevent future harm.
Our work on Future Risk explores alternative futures and analyses their potential impact by discussing their associated risk factors and opportunities, as well as identifying possible interventions.
In this way, we aim to help EU policymakers gain knowledge that they can act upon, and work together to develop anticipatory, long-term approaches to policymaking.
From climate to technology, policy decisions need to be made today despite long-term uncertainty. Foresight processes can help to develop an anticipatory culture within the European Commission.
Structured group exercises help to create a shared space for exploring alternative futures, testing assumptions and discussing potential problems, solutions and opportunities in a focused way.
Tools that we have developed are ready to use in workshops: they cover future scenarios and large-scale trends, systems-mapping exercises, games and themed toolkits.
Together, these tools aim to make foresight more tangible and practically useful in the decision-making process.

European democracies are being affected by rapid technological, social and political change. Policymakers need to anticipate emerging risks and opportunities to ensure that democratic institutions remain resilient, inclusive and responsive to citizens’ needs.

Foresight methods can help to explore plausible future developments, enabling decision-makers to understand uncertainties, test policy choices and prepare for long-term challenges before they materialise.

Our report on the futures of EU democracy presents a foresight study, using expert workshops and scenario development to examine how artificial intelligence, citizen participation and democratic governance could evolve under different future conditions.

The findings help policymakers to reflect on key trade-offs, including between efficiency, citizen agency, data use and the concentration of power, supporting more resilient and future-oriented approaches to democratic governance.

Policy decisions often rely on incomplete evidence, making it difficult to understand the real-world impacts of interventions across labour markets, health systems and public spending, leading to inefficient or misdirected policy choices over time.

Research using causal and microeconomic methods helps to isolate what works by comparing outcomes under different policy scenarios, improving confidence in decisions and reducing uncertainty in complex socio-economic environments.

We provide practical tools such as evaluation repositories, forecasting models, and sample size calculators, supporting structured impact assessment and enabling consistent, comparable analysis across different policy areas and countries.

These tools help the European Commission and Member States to improve the quality of policy evaluation, strengthen accountability, and design more effective interventions based on measurable results rather than assumptions.

Governments need reliable evidence on the effects of public policies to improve outcomes, ensure that spending is effective, and support better regulation. Robust evaluation helps to identify the interventions that are having meaningful results.

Advanced econometric and impact evaluation methods can be used to measure policy effects, improve evaluation practices, and strengthen the evidence base for decisions across a wide range of policy areas.
We provide a wide range of research tools, analysis and publications that support causal policy evaluation and data-driven analysis across the European Union.

Our aim is to support EU institutions and Member States by providing scientific expertise, fostering collaboration between researchers and policymakers, and building capacity for high-quality policy evaluation and evidence-informed decision-making.

Policymakers need reliable evidence on whether public interventions are having their intended outcomes. Understanding real-world impacts helps to improve programme design, ensure that resources are allocated effectively, and support more informed policy decisions.

Rigorous evaluation methods can be used to estimate the causal effects of policies, distinguishing genuine impacts from other factors and providing evidence on what works, for whom, and under what conditions.

Our policy evaluation map shows national-level impact evaluations that have been carried out by the Joint Research Centre across policy areas including employment, education, social inclusion, agriculture and competition, including both completed and ongoing studies.

Our aim is to support European Commission services and Member States by strengthening policy evaluation, promoting evidence-informed decision-making, and encouraging the use of robust methods across diverse policy areas.

Involving citizens can improve policymaking, strengthen public trust, and increase democratic legitimacy. But achieving lasting benefits depends on how this participation is designed, supported and integrated into decision-making processes.
Research can help in assessing the impacts of citizen engagement on policies, institutions and society, identifying the conditions that help participation to have successful outcomes.

Our report on the impact of citizen engagement analyses survey and interview evidence from public administrations and experts across 20 EU countries, examining how citizen engagement influences policymaking, institutional culture, democratic processes and collaboration between citizens, policymakers and civil society.

The findings highlight practical factors that can increase impact, including political commitment, effective communication and follow-up on recommendations, providing evidence to help policymakers design more effective and accountable citizen participation processes.

column2: Training in citizen engagement for public administrations: overview
plcBriefme: Citizen participation forms an integral part of effective policymaking, especially for governments in the design of policies that reflect diverse public needs at the local, regional and national level, as well as for building trust with communities and preserving legitimacy.

column2: Training in citizen engagement for public administrations: overview
plcBriefme: Research and training in participatory and deliberative democracy helps policymakers to understand how to design inclusive engagement processes, improve methods of policy co-creation and strengthen democratic resilience through structured participation and dialogue.

column2: Training in citizen engagement for public administrations: overview
plcBriefme: Our programme provides online training for public administrations on citizen engagement, combining self-paced learning with moderated sessions and practical exercises.

column2: Training in citizen engagement for public administrations: overview
plcBriefme: It supports EU efforts to strengthen democratic institutions by building skills in participatory policymaking, enabling administrations to implement structured engagement processes and embed citizen input in decision-making.

column2: Learning and development in evidence-informed policymaking
plcBriefme: Policymaking can become more effective and impactful when it is informed by evidence. Strengthening the skills involved in the process of acquiring and using evidence throughout the policy cycle helps policymakers to develop more robust policies, respond to complex challenges, and reinforce public trust in decision-making.

column2: Learning and development in evidence-informed policymaking
plcBriefme: Training materials (both for scientists and policymakers) can help in identifying the knowledge, skills and practices that are needed for stronger collaboration for evidence-informed policymaking (EIPM). It also supports practical approaches for communicating evidence, assessing research and considering it throughout the policymaking process.

column2: Learning and development in evidence-informed policymaking
plcBriefme: We bring together two competence frameworks (one for policymakers, one for scientists), training materials, e-learning and professional development programmes, designed to strengthen evidence-informed policymaking and science-for-policy practice across Europe.

column2: Learning and development in evidence-informed policymaking
plcBriefme: By doing so we aim to support policymakers and researchers at the EIPM interface, by providing theoretical models, guidance and learning tools that can improve the use of evidence, build institutional capacity, and strengthen collaboration between science and public policy.

Effective science-for-policy work requires a range of competences, including understanding evidence, assessing information and applying it in policymaking contexts, which can vary widely between individuals and roles.

Policymakers and researchers can benefit from understanding the full range of competences involved in Science4Policy, and identifying their strengths and areas for improvement in engaging with policy-relevant evidence.

Smart4Policy is an online self-reflection tool that helps users to assess their competences (whether as scientists or as policymakers) against the two established EU frameworks for innovative policymaking and science-for-policy work.
It provides personalised feedback, suggestions and resources for development, helping users to plan their learning and improve their ability to work effectively with evidence in policy contexts.

column2: European Community of Practice on evidence-informed policymaking
plcBriefme: Effective use of evidence to inform policymaking involves collaboration between researchers, policymakers, knowledge brokers and other stakeholders. Building strong professional networks helps to address practical challenges, and improves the way that evidence is used in policymaking.

column2: European Community of Practice on evidence-informed policymaking
plcBriefme: Research can help to identify effective ways of strengthening evidence ecosystems, supporting collaboration across organisations, and sharing practical experience around the use of scientific knowledge and other kinds of evidence in public policymaking in different contexts.

column2: European Community of Practice on evidence-informed policymaking
plcBriefme: The European Community of Practice on EIPM brings together experienced professionals working on evidence-informed policymaking, through meetings, webinars, discussions and collaborative projects focused on knowledge exchange and finding practical solutions.

column2: European Community of Practice on evidence-informed policymaking
plcBriefme: The community aims to strengthen institutional capacity by helping practitioners to share lessons, address common challenges, and develop approaches that improve the consistent use of evidence in policymaking across Europe.

Democratic systems across Europe are facing growing pressure from political, economic, social and technological change, alongside declining levels of trust and increasing polarisation in many societies.
These challenges affect how effectively democracies respond to citizens’ needs and maintain their legitimacy, making resilience and public trust central policy concerns.
This project analyses key drivers shaping democratic resilience, drawing on research to identify current challenges and explore ways to strengthen democratic institutions and citizen engagement.
It supports policymakers by mapping risks, examining emerging trends and identifying approaches that can help build more resilient, adaptive and trusted democratic systems.
EU policy decisions rely on simulation models that test the impacts of legislation. Transparency and scrutiny are essential for trust and accountability across complex policy domains.

Research in modelling systems helps policymakers to compare scenarios, assess the impacts of proposed laws and improve the quality of decisions by making assumptions, data and uncertainties explicit and open to review.

MIDAS is the European Commission’s inventory of policy models, documenting tools that are used in impact assessments and linking them with data, publications and policy actions in a searchable system.

It supports the EU Better Regulation agenda by ensuring that models used in policymaking are transparent, documented and accessible, strengthening evidence-informed decision making and stakeholder confidence in regulatory processes.

Food fraud is any intentional deception of consumers around food. It can involve replacing more expensive ingredients with cheaper ones, lying about the origin of food or production processes, or tampering with records such as best-by dates. Food fraud undermines consumer trust, safety and fair markets. It can distort prices, harm legitimate producers and mislead consumers about what they are eating and where it comes from.
Research can help to detect patterns in fraud, and identify the food categories that are most prone to fraud.
We compile data around food fraud incidents world-wide. This data can be used to better target official controls of food that is most at risk of fraud, because of its type or origin.

Our work supports policymakers, regulators and industry by helping to improve the monitoring and prevention of fraud, and the enforcement of anti-fraud measures, across food supply chains at the national, EU and global level.

Monitoring frameworks help to translate policy goals into measurable indicators, making it easier to identify progress, compare performance, highlight implementation gaps and support evidence-informed decision-making around biodiversity protection and ecosystem restoration.

The EU Biodiversity Strategy Dashboard monitors progress towards the EU’s 2030 biodiversity targets, helping policymakers to assess whether conservation, restoration and sustainable land and sea management efforts are on track across the EU and in Member States.

This dashboard brings together regularly updated indicators covering protected areas, ecosystem restoration, sustainable agriculture, pollution, forests, freshwater, marine ecosystems and biodiversity financing, using data from EU institutions, Member States and scientific monitoring programmes.

By providing a common evidence base, the dashboard supports policy implementation, progress reporting and evaluation of the EU Biodiversity Strategy, while helping to identify where additional action or improved monitoring is needed.
